issues.quote: She keeps it so on purpose, so that nothing is ever late.
issues.fact: L4 gives only that Rosa's clock was exactly fifteen minutes fast. It says nothing about why or whether the clock is kept fast on purpose.
issues.misreading: A solver could read the deliberate setting as a sign that Rosa's clock is a fixed, known offset that the kitchen readings should be trusted to follow, or that the 'fast' figure is a policy rather than a measured fact. Neither is in the sheet.

issues.quote: He meant it to strike the first minute of the new century, and he was very exact about every part of it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the repeater, its purpose, or its dating. The sentence adds a claim about when the watch was meant to strike.
issues.misreading: A solver could take the repeater to be a timing device with a specific intended date or moment, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: A person who knows the sound can tell the time from it in the dark.
issues.fact: The fact sheet contains no information about how the repeater sounds or how time can be read from it.
issues.misreading: This introduces a method for reading the time by sound that the sheet does not give. A solver could treat it as a clue about how a sounded time could be known in darkness, which goes beyond the facts.

issues.fact: The sheet says only that the master made everyone show their watches at nine. It does not say this happens every year.
issues.misreading: The phrase suggests a routine or habit, which implies the watch check was an expected ritual rather than a one-off event that evening.
